spots.title: Ridgehawks Club Fair
spots.text: Every club at North Valley has a folding table, a banner, and someone who wants your email. There's a cooler of free burritos at the end of the row.

choices.label: Work the tables — meet people
choices.reaction: You sign up for three newsletters you'll never read and learn the names of half your floor. When you mention Jordan, everybody already knows him. Of course they do.

choices.label: Grab free burritos and sit in the sun
choices.reaction: Two burritos, one bench, zero obligations. Cheap calories count. You feel like a person again.

spots.title: Bench on the Quad
spots.text: A sun-warm bench facing the center plaza. Students cut across in every direction, all of them late for something.

choices.label: Sit for a while and people-watch
choices.reaction: You let the campus happen around you for an hour. A frisbee lands at your feet twice. Nobody needs anything from you. It's great.

choices.label: Call home
choices.reaction: Your mom answers on the first ring and asks if you're eating vegetables. Your dad gets on and asks one question: 'You sign up for that tryout?' You hang up feeling twelve feet tall and slightly guilty about the burritos.

spots.title: Your Bed
spots.text: Extra-long twin. The mattress is plastic-wrapped and smells like a warehouse. It's still the best thing in the room.

choices.label: Take a nap
choices.reaction: You close your eyes for 'five minutes' and wake up with the sheet pattern printed on your face. Your legs thank you.

choices.label: Go to sleep
choices.reaction: You're out in four minutes. Somewhere down the hall someone is losing a video game very loudly. You don't hear it.

spots.title: Your Desk
spots.text: A desk lamp, a Kinesiology textbook still in its shrink-wrap, and a planner you promised yourself you'd use.

choices.label: Study for an hour
choices.reaction: Muscle fiber types. Energy systems. Half of this is literally about your own body, which helps. You fill four pages of notes.

choices.label: Study late, then crash
choices.reaction: You read until your eyes cross. At midnight Jordan tosses you a granola bar without a word. You sleep, but not enough.

spots.title: Moreno Hall 104 — Intro to Kinesiology
spots.text: Professor Okafor's lecture hall. Sixty seats, and the front row is always empty.

choices.label: Sit in on the opening lecture
choices.reaction: Professor Okafor doesn't do syllabus day. You leave with actual notes, an assignment due Friday, and one useful fact: she gives athletes zero special treatment, and she says it like a warning.

choices.label: Attend lecture
choices.reaction: Okafor walks the aisles while she talks, which makes it impossible to zone out. Today: why your heart rate lies to you in the fourth quarter. You take good notes.

choices.label: Go to office hours
choices.reaction: You're the only one there. Okafor seems almost pleased. She walks you through the Friday material twice, then says, 'Most of your classmates will learn this Thursday night. Badly.'

choices.label: Review notes in the empty hall
choices.reaction: The lecture hall at night is weirdly peaceful. You copy the week's diagrams onto the whiteboard and explain them to nobody. It works.

pass.reaction: Question four is the heart-rate thing from Tuesday. Question nine is the energy-systems chart you drew on the whiteboard. You walk out ten minutes early. Okafor glances up as you leave and gives you the smallest nod in academic history.

fail.reaction: You recognize maybe half the words. You guess on the energy-systems chart and leave two short answers blank. On your way out, Okafor says quietly, 'Athletes who want to stay eligible come to office hours.' It isn't a threat. It's worse — it's advice.

spots.title: Rec Center — Court 1
spots.text: Hardwood, eight hoops, and the squeak of somebody else's game on the far court. A rack of balls sits by the baseline.

choices.label: Shootaround — work on your shot
choices.reaction: You grab a rack and get up shots until your form stops lying to you.

choices.label: Jump into the pickup run
choices.reaction: The run is faster than anything from high school. You hold your own — a couple of buckets, one chase-down block that gets an 'OHHH' from the sideline. Somebody in a North Valley polo watches the last game from the doorway, says nothing, and leaves.

spots.title: Conditioning Corner
spots.text: Racks, a rowing machine with a sign that says DO NOT DROP THE HANDLE, and a whiteboard with someone's brutal circuit still on it.

choices.label: Run the circuit on the whiteboard
choices.reaction: Rows, box jumps, sled pushes, repeat. By round three you understand why someone wrote it in red marker. You finish. Barely. That's the point.

choices.label: Foam roll and stretch
choices.reaction: Twenty minutes on a foam roller, discovering muscles you didn't know you had by how much they hate you. You walk out looser than you walked in.
